body:
**Bear phase and Harshad Mehta**
- In the early 1990s Damani was short while Mehta pushed the market to new highs. Both kept betting in opposite directions until Mehta's diversion of bank money was exposed and the market crashed. He "clashed with Mehta twice" and came out on top both times. Later he shorted the stocks Mehta promoted as an adviser (BPL, Videocon, Sterlite) "until they fell". — [Rediff, 2017](https://www.rediff.com/business/special/how-well-do-you-know-d-marts-damani/20170405.htm)
- Wikipedia (citing ET 2014 and Business Standard 2017) says he made large profits by short-selling stocks Mehta had inflated, in connection with the 1992 scam. — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radhakishan_Damani)
- Secondary blogs say he later admitted a delay of "even a week" would have bankrupted him. That means the short was near-fatal under margin pressure before the scam broke. They also say he was accused of price hammering after the scam and later cleared. — [Tickertape blog summary](https://www.tickertape.in/blog/10-fascinating-facts-about-radhakishan-damani-the-self-made-billionaire/); [completetradersedge (blog)](https://completetradersedge.com/radhakishan-damani-dmart-avenue-supermarts/). UNVERIFIED / FOLKLORE: I found no primary source for the "one week from bankruptcy" quote or the "clean chit".
- "Bear cartel": blogs say Manu Manek ("the Cobra") ran a bear cartel whose famous associates were the "3 R's" (Rakesh Jhunjhunwala, Radhakishan Damani, Raju "Chartist"). — [Finology Insider (blog)](https://insider.finology.in/investing/manu-manek-cobra-of-stock-market); [Trade Brains (blog)](https://tradebrains.in/manu-manek-aka-cobra-of-stock-market). FOLKLORE: widely repeated but not confirmed in mainstream press or SEBI documents I could access. Sucheta Dalal's reporting is the likely original source and was not checked.

**Mentors**
- Several sources say Damani regarded Chandrakant Sampat ("father of Indian value investing", died 2015) as his mentor and moved from speculation toward long-term investing under his influence. — [Equentis (blog)](https://www.equentis.com/blog/investors-in-share-market-in-india/); [Wikipedia: Chandrakant Sampat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandrakant_Sampat); [PPFAS on Sampat](https://amc.ppfas.com/media/quotes/chandrakant-sampat-a-life-spent-spotting-value-in-indian-markets.php). Mostly secondary. Treat the details of the relationship as loosely sourced.
- Jhunjhunwala named Damani as one of his mentors in 2019. — [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/rakesh-jhunjunwala-guru-radhakishan-damani-second-richest-mukesh-ambani/story/396422.html)

`theme:sector-real-estate` · confidence: single-source · tickers: DLF, GODREJPROP, OBEROIRLTY, PRESTIGE, LODHA, PHOENIXLTD, BRIGADE, SOBHA

**How it makes money:** Land -> approvals -> presale -> construction cash cycle; annuity rentals for commercial/malls.

**Metrics that matter:**
- Presales value/volume
- Collections & OCF
- Net debt / equity
- Launches & GDV pipeline
- Realisation per sq ft
- Embedded EBITDA margin
- Inventory overhang (months)
- Annuity: occupancy, rent growth

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Landowner (JD/JV) -> developer (approvals, brand, execution) -> contractors -> buyer (home loan via banks/HFCs). Land holders and branded developers capture most value in upcycles; contractors earn thin margins; channel partners take 2–4%.

**Cycle drivers:** Rates, affordability, regulation, funding liquidity, office hiring, wealth effect, unsold inventory.

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- ANAROCK / PropEquity quarterly sales & launches
- Knight Frank Mumbai monthly property registrations
- RBI housing credit growth
- RERA project registrations
- Office absorption (JLL/CBRE quarterly)

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: deleveraged balance sheets, delivery record, brand, asset-light JD/JV land, cash-flow focus. Losers: land-banking on debt, customer-advance diversion, construction delays.

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** P/NAV (0.5x troughs 2013–19 → 1.5–2x 2021–24 peaks) or P/B. 2007 peak: realty index fell ~80–90% into 2009 and stayed depressed until ~2020.

**Current state (Nov 2026):** ANAROCK Q3 CY26 (Jul–Sep 2026): top-7 city sales ~1,00,220 units (+3% YoY) after Q2 CY26 ~90,700 (−6% YoY, West Asia conflict); PropEquity reported −6% to 103,000 for the September quarter. Realty led the sector rally on 17 Nov 2026 (HDFC Sky snapshot).

**Classic traps:**
- Presales inflated by subvention/discount schemes
- NAV built on land bank that never launches
- P&L-based P/E (meaningless due to completion accounting)
- Buying at peak launch activity

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:INFY:q3fy27-guidance-midpoint-raised`
- **Method:** base rate · **P(ours)** 0.55 · **P(base)** 0.70 · resolve by 2027-01-31
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 (Oct-2026): FY27 cc guidance cut from 1.5–3% to 1–2%; op-margin guide 20–22% kept (Q2 ~21%). Q2 cc growth +1.5% YoY, +1.2% QoQ; H1 +1.9% cc. Mgmt cites soft volumes, pricing pressure/AI deflation, weak Retail/Hi-Tech, rate rises; large deals TCV $8.8 bn. Infosys history at Q3: midpoint raised in FY23, FY25 and FY26, unchanged (narrowed) in FY24.
- **Why our number differs from base:** H1 at 1.9% means the 1–2% band already embeds a weak H2; Q3 has furloughs, and they just cut. A narrow-upward revision (e.g., 1.5–2%) is plausible but so is a hold. Below the historical base because this year's direction of revision was down.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Infosys raised the guidance midpoint at Q3 in ~3 of the last 4 years.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if the FY27 cc revenue guidance announced with Q3 FY27 results has a midpoint strictly greater than 1.5% (e.g., 1.5–2.0% or 1.75–2.25%). Hold at 1–2% or any cut = NO.
- **Resolution source:** Infosys Q3 FY27 press release / fact sheet (infosys.com, NSE)
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/Infosys_28102026173824_SE_filing_Earnings_call_transcript.pdf
